title: 2025年真题 · 完形填空
passage:
There are many understandable reasons why you might find it difficult to ask for help when you need it. Psychologists have been interested in this ___1___ for decades, not least because people's widespread ___2___ to ask for help has led to some high-profile failures.
Asking for help takes ___3___ . It involves communicating a need on your part—there's something you can't do. ___4___ you're broadcasting your own weaknesses, which can be ___5___ . You might worry about coming across as incompetent. You might have ___6___ about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with. ___7___ someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts. Yet another ___8___ that you might be worried about is being a nuisance or ___9___ the person you go to for help.
If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to ___10___ for help because you have the added worry of the other person ___11___ your request. You might see such refusals as implying something ___12___ about the status of your relationship with them. To ___13___ these difficulties, try to remind yourself that everyone needs help sometimes. Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves. And while you might ___14___ coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are ___15___ as more competent, not less.
Perhaps most encouraging of all is a paper from 2022 by researchers at Stanford University that involved a mix of contrived help-seeking interactions and asking people to ___16___ times they'd sought help in the past. The findings showed that help-seekers generally underestimate how ___17___ other people will be to help and how good it'll make the help-giver feel (for most people, having the chance to help someone is highly ___18___ ).
So, bear all this in mind the next time you need to ask for help. ___19___ take care over who you ask and when you ask them. And if someone can't help right now, avoid taking it personally. They might just be too ___20___ , or they might not feel confident about their ability to help.
passage_zh:
当你需要帮助时却发现难以开口求助，这有许多可以理解的原因。几十年来,心理学家一直对这个问题很感兴趣,尤其是因为人们普遍不愿求助已经导致了一些备受瞩目的失败案例。
寻求帮助需要勇气。这涉及到传达你自身的需求——有些事情你做不到。换句话说,你在暴露自己的弱点,这可能会让人不舒服。你可能会担心给人留下无能的印象。你可能会担心失去对所求助事项的控制权。一旦有人开始帮忙,也许他们会接管一切,或者把你之前的努力归功于自己。你可能担心的另一个因素是给你求助的人添麻烦或带来不便。
如果你在自尊心低落方面有困扰,你可能会发现寻求帮助特别困难,因为你还要额外担心对方会拒绝你的请求。你可能会将这种拒绝视为暗示你与他们的关系存在某种负面问题。为了克服这些困难,试着提醒自己每个人有时都需要帮助。没有人无所不知、无所不能。虽然你可能担心给人留下无能的印象,但实际上有研究表明,寻求建议的人被认为更有能力,而非更无能。
也许最令人鼓舞的是Stanford University研究人员2022年发表的一篇论文,该研究结合了精心设计的求助互动和让人们回忆过去求助经历的方式。研究结果显示,求助者通常会低估他人愿意提供帮助的程度,以及这会让帮助者感觉有多好(对大多数人来说,有机会帮助他人是非常有价值的回报)。
因此,下次你需要寻求帮助时,请记住所有这些。同时要注意你向谁求助以及何时求助。如果有人现在无法提供帮助,不要往心里去。他们可能只是太忙了,或者他们可能对自己提供帮助的能力不够自信。

title: 2025年真题 · 新题型（段落小标题）
intro: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

paras.text: Great ideas don't stand alone. In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted. To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits. In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.
paras.explain: 要反复宣传、为主意争取认同

paras.text: Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first. But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders. When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, "Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth."
paras.explain: 经由同事、部门等渠道去推进

paras.text: One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded. Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all. So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant. Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in future discussions. So, instead of saying, "Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated," you could try, "Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might be able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers."
paras.explain: 别自以为是，要谦逊倾听

paras.text: New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones. In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out. Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time. Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.

When pitching a new idea, it's important to use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit. Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal. For example, try, "I can see lots of applications for this new approach" rather than, "This innovation is the only way." Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
paras.explain: 用正面语言而非负面语言

passage:
Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution. However, it takes more than simply having a good idea. How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself. Why? Because writing a new script—literally or figuratively—means that other team members will have to adapt to something new. Not to mention, if the process you're scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings. To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:
___41___
Great ideas don't stand alone. In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted. To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits. In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.
___42___
Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first. But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders. When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, "Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth."
___43___
One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded. Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all. So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant. Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in future discussions. So, instead of saying, "Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated," you could try, "Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might be able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers."
___44___
New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones. In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out. Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time. Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.
___45___
When pitching a new idea, it's important to use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit. Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal. For example, try, "I can see lots of applications for this new approach" rather than, "This innovation is the only way." Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
passage_zh:
每个人都想成为那样的人——能够看到与其他人相同的信息，却能看出新颖创新的解决方案。然而，这不仅仅需要有一个好主意。你如何分享它与建议本身同样重要。为什么？因为编写新脚本——无论是字面意义上还是比喻意义上——意味着其他团队成员将不得不适应新事物。更不用说，如果你要废弃的流程是别人提出的，就有可能伤害感情。要让人们认可一个创新的新想法，请遵循以下步骤：
做一名推销员。
好主意不会独立存在。换句话说，你不能只提一次建议就期望它被采纳。要看到改变，你需要为你的计划摇旗呐喊并推销其优点。此外，你需要愿意经受审查和批评，并准备好以不同方式向不同受众解释你的创新。
利用渠道。
有时先去找老板是有道理的。但在其他时候，在同事或其他利益相关者中建立联盟是有用的。当这种方法奏效时，效果会很好——因为你已经准备好应对固执上司的反对,可以这样回答："事实上,我联系了技术部门的几个人,讨论了这类网站更新需要多少时间,他们表示有时间处理。"
保持谦逊。
获得认可的最大障碍之一是当想法的提出者被视为好争辩、防御性强或思想封闭时。因为,说实话:没有人喜欢万事通。所以,如果人们不同意你的观点,不要愤愤不平。相反,充分倾听他们的担忧,试着理解他们的观点,并在未来的讨论中纳入他们的担忧(以及可能的补救措施)。因此,与其说"Martha,我们目前的口号令人困惑,应该更新",你可以尝试说"Martha提出了一个很好的观点,我们目前的口号对利益相关者来说有着悠久的历史,但我想知道我们是否可以集思广益,想出一个能在此基础上发展的标语——并且对新客户来说更清晰。"
尊重过去。
新想法是旧想法的孙辈。换句话说,不要为了让你的改进脱颖而出而贬低旧的解决方案。请记住,鉴于旧系统解决的任何问题——或者也许是近期未能解决的问题——它在当时是一个好主意。在你提出未来创新时赞赏以往的贡献有助于增强你想法的可信度。
保持积极。
在提出新想法时,使用富足的语言而不是缺陷的语言很重要。与其说什么是错误的、破碎的或不理想的,不如谈论什么是正确的、可修复的或理想的。例如,试着说"我能看到这种新方法有很多应用",而不是"这个创新是唯一的方法"。保持乐观但现实,你就会脱颖而出。

title: 2025年真题 · 翻译
intro: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
passage:
You know the moment—the conversation slows, then there's a pause. It's awkward, and so awkward that some people will panic and say anything. Do we all find such silences so stressful?
Researchers analysed the frequency and impact of gaps greater than 2 seconds during conversations, including an overview of previous studies which indicate that the fear of awkward silences can be so extreme that people avoid talking to strangers, even though doing so is likely to be an enjoyable experience.
During conversations with short gaps, people feel more connected to their conversation partners. But such feelings of connection markedly dip when entering a long gap. Long gaps between strangers are likely to be followed by a change in topic.
But the opposite seems to be true for conversations between friends. Long gaps there saw increased connection. Between friends, longer gaps seem to provide natural moments for reflection and expression.
passage_zh:
你一定遇到过这种情况——对话渐渐冷场，接着出现一阵停顿。这种停顿让人很尴尬，尴尬得有人会一下慌了神，随口乱说点什么。可是，我们真的都觉得这种沉默那么让人难受吗？
围绕这一问题，研究者分析了对话中超过 2 秒的停顿出现的频率和造成的影响，其中还包括对此前研究的综述：这些研究表明，人们对尴尬沉默的害怕可能极端到让他们干脆回避和陌生人交谈，尽管和陌生人聊聊往往会是一段愉快的体验。
研究发现，在停顿较短的对话中，人们会觉得自己与对话对方更亲近。但是，一旦对话进入较长的停顿，这种亲近感就会明显减弱。陌生人之间一旦出现较长的停顿，接下来往往就会换个话题。
但在朋友之间的对话里，情况似乎正好相反——长停顿反而带来了更强的亲近感。在朋友之间，较长的停顿反而成了一种自然的契机，让彼此沉下来思考，也把想说的话表达出来。

title: 2025年真题 · 小作文
prompt: Suppose you are planning a short play based on a classic Chinese novel. Write your friend John an email to1) introduce the play, and2) invite him to take part in it.Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.Do not use your own name in your email; Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
tips: 2025年考研英语二真题 写作的中心立意是本邮件要达成的交际目的：把我筹备的这部改编自中国古典名著的短剧介绍给 John，并诚恳邀请他出演其中一个角色。它同时兜住了 introduce the play 和 invite him to take part in it 两个任务。可展开的要点：介绍这部 short play based on a classic Chinese novel：说清改编自
sample:
Dear John,I hope this email finds you well. I am now planning a short play based on the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West, and I want to tell you about it. The play retells how the Monkey King protects his master on the journey west, showing courage and loyalty.I am writing to invite you to take part in it. With your rich stage experience, you would be perfect for the role of the Monkey King. We will start rehearsing next week. Could you please reply and let me know whether you can join us?Looking forward to your reply.
Yours,
Li Ming

title: 2025年真题 · 大作文
prompt: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your essay, you should1) describe and interpret the chart, and2) give your comments.Write your answer in about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
tips: 2025年考研英语二真题 写作的中心立意是全篇中心：图表显示看电视、散步这类省力活动主导了老年人的日常休闲，而下棋、养花等费神活动参与度低，这一失衡现象值得社会关注并加以引导。可展开的要点：第一块内容：读出 看电视 最高 90.8%、下棋 最低 18.4% 及中间项，构成对图表的客观描述；第二块内容：概括规律并分析成因——省力、低成本、不需伙伴的活动更受欢迎，费体力或需搭档的活动参与度自然偏低；第
sample: The bar chart clearly illustrates the main leisure activities of the elderly in a certain community. As is shown, watching TV ranks far ahead of the rest, chosen by 90.8% of the respondents, followed by taking a walk at 68.3%. By contrast, growing flowers and reading account for only 34.7% and 31.8% respectively, while playing chess sits at the bottom, favored by merely 18.4%.These figures reveal that passive and effortless pastimes clearly dominate the daily lives of senior citizens. Watching TV and walking cost little and demand neither special skills nor companions, so they naturally appeal to the majority. In contrast, hobbies such as chess or gardening require more energy, patience or partners, which explains their limited popularity.In my view, this pattern deserves our attention. Physical and social activities benefit the health of the elderly far more than sitting before a screen. Therefore, communities should organize richer events to encourage older people to step outside and enjoy a more colorful later life.
